extracted.intended_audience: Authors, reviewers, and editors involved with submissions to the Proceedings of the London Mathematical Society
extracted.subtask_description: Policy and procedural guidelines for how submissions to the Proceedings of the London Mathematical Society are assessed, reviewed, revised, and decided upon, including reviewer anonymity, editorial stages, integrity checks, transfers, appeals, and timelines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Single-anonymous peer review
rubrics_metrics.description: The Proceedings of the London Mathematical Society operates a single-anonymous peer review process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewer identity is not made visible to author; author identity is visible to reviewer; reviewer and author identity are both visible to the editor. The Reviewers interact only with the editor and/or journal team. Reviewers do not interact with each other or with the authors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Non-discrimination in assessment
rubrics_metrics.description: Articles are assessed on their intellectual content without regard to sex, gender identity, disability, age, nationality, race, ethnicity, sexual orientation, belief system, neurodiversity, political philosophy, or socioeconomic status.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This follows the London Mathematical Society’s Ethical Policy for Journals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Stage 1 — Assessment by editor (suitability)
rubrics_metrics.description: Submissions are initially assessed by an editor, who determines whether the paper is suitable for further consideration by the journal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submissions may be rejected by the editor at this stage if judged to be unsuitable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Stage 2 — Expert advice on mathematical and editorial standards
rubrics_metrics.description: The editor will send the submission to several independent experts who will advise whether, in their opinion, the paper is likely to meet the mathematical and editorial standards of the Proceedings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The editor may ask the author(s) to revise their paper based on the advice of the expert(s).

rubrics_metrics.name: Stage 3 — Editorial Board approval to proceed
rubrics_metrics.description: The advice of the experts is reported to the Editorial Board and a decision is taken as to whether to proceed with peer review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submissions may be rejected at this stage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Stage 4 — Full peer review (in-depth reviewer reports)
rubrics_metrics.description: The editor will obtain an in‐depth report on the paper from one or more reviewers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This constitutes the main detailed evaluation of the manuscript.

rubrics_metrics.name: Stage 5 — Editor recommendation based on reviewer reports
rubrics_metrics.description: The editor receives the reviewer’s report and makes a decision about how to proceed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The editor may ask the author to revise their paper based on the report. If the reviewer’s report is not positive, or identifies a major problem with the work, then the submission will be rejected.

rubrics_metrics.name: Stage 6 — Editorial decision by Board
rubrics_metrics.description: The editor will make a publication recommendation to the Editorial Board, who will agree whether the paper should be accepted, revised further, or rejected.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Final publication decision is taken with Editorial Board agreement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Revisions and follow-up reports
rubrics_metrics.description: If revisions are requested, the editor may obtain further reports from the reviewers about the revisions before returning to stage 6.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Editors may iteratively seek reviewer feedback on revised versions prior to a final decision.

rubrics_metrics.name: Manuscript transfer to other LMS journals
rubrics_metrics.description: If an article is not accepted for publication in the Proceedings, the editors may offer the author the opportunity to transfer their submission to other suitable journals published by the London Mathematical Society.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The offer to transfer is at editors' discretion and may be made prior to or after full peer review. If accepted after peer review, the paper will be transferred along with any advice or reviewer reports obtained during the review process. Authors may accept or decline the offer.

rubrics_metrics.name: Peer review times and efficiency
rubrics_metrics.description: The Proceedings aims to provide a fair, rigorous and efficient peer review process; editors strive to review papers with the least possible delay.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Editors must balance respect for volunteer reviewers with authors' needs and expectations. If a submission is to be rejected, editors aim to do so at the earliest opportunity so authors may submit elsewhere. Final decision time varies depending on paper length and subject area. On rare occasions, if reviewers cannot be found or reports are not obtained, the editor may offer the author the option to withdraw the paper. Authors retain the right to withdraw at any time during the review process.

rubrics_metrics.name: Standard for submissions claiming solutions to famous problems
rubrics_metrics.description: Submissions purporting to solve famous open problems or theorems will only be considered if the argument is exceptionally clear, complete and precise.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submissions which appear implausible are rejected quickly. It is incumbent upon authors to provide convincing proofs, and not upon the journal to find errors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research integrity screening
rubrics_metrics.description: The Proceedings may use third-party tools to screen submissions for research integrity issues.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Screening can include checks for plagiarism, duplicate submission, or similarity with fraudulent paper mill submissions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appeals policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors are entitled to appeal against a rejection decision where it is clear that the decision was based on a factual error in the review process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Decisions based on editorial judgement of novelty or significance may not be appealed. More information is available in the Ethical Policy for Journals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Neutrality of publication
rubrics_metrics.description: Publication of individual authors' work does not constitute endorsement by the London Mathematical Society of the policies or actions of any government or other agencies.
